seoTitle: Fix 'Rule Conflicting with DNS Record' in Squarespace
metaDescription: Resolve the Squarespace domain forwarding error about a conflicting DNS record by finding and removing the record that's blocking your rule.
intro: When setting up domain forwarding in Squarespace, you may hit an error saying a forwarding rule conflicts with an existing DNS record. This happens because Squarespace won't let you forward a subdomain that still has an A record or CNAME pointing somewhere else. Here's how to clear the conflict and get forwarding working.

steps.heading: Understand the cause
steps.body: When you try to forward a subdomain like www, Squarespace checks for existing DNS records tied to it. If an A record, CNAME, or custom record already exists there, it blocks the new forwarding rule.

steps.heading: Open your DNS settings
steps.body: Go to Settings, then Domains, choose your domain, and scroll down to DNS Settings to see the full list of records.

steps.heading: Find the conflicting record
steps.body: Look for any CNAME or A record under the subdomain you're trying to forward — most commonly the www record.

steps.heading: Delete the conflicting record
steps.body: Click the trash icon next to that DNS entry to remove its current mapping.

steps.heading: Re-add the forwarding rule
steps.body: Go back to Forwarding settings and add the rule again — it should now save without the conflict error.

faq.question: Why does Squarespace say my forwarding rule conflicts with a DNS record?
faq.answer: It's because an existing A record or CNAME is already assigned to the subdomain you're trying to forward, and Squarespace won't overwrite it automatically.

faq.question: Which record usually causes the conflict?
faq.answer: In most cases it's the www CNAME record, though root domain forwarding can also conflict with default A records.

faq.question: Is it safe to delete the conflicting DNS record?
faq.answer: Yes — once forwarding is active, you no longer need the old A or CNAME record it was replacing.

faq.question: What if I'm forwarding my root domain?
faq.answer: You may need to remove multiple conflicting A records, usually the default Squarespace ones, before the rule will save.
